title: Radial rollout runway checklist and digest (oct 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, field-focused runbook for the ‘Radial’ rollout (Oct 2026). It bundles the preflight checklist, a 7-day calendar view with cutover windows, quick rollback recipes, and a raw draft of user-facing release notes. Goal is a single page operators can reference during a tight 48h launch window.

Scope and constraints:
- Affects hosting/edge routing, model-routing logic, and batching pipeline. No schema or DB migrations.
- Target traffic ramp: 0 -> 10% -> 35% -> 70% -> 100% across 5 steps (4h between steps, subject to telemetry).
- Canary region: us-west1; failover region: us-east4.
- Capacity: Dedicated pool alpha-3 (8xA100), burst to beta-1 for first 2h only.

Preflight checklist (must-complete items before first traffic shift):
1) Code & infra
   - [ ] Merge blocking PRs and confirm green CI (GH PR 5812).
   - [ ] Verify infra diff no rolling restart required (infra PR ID in linked_artifacts).
2) Configs & flags
   - [ ] Feature flag radial-rollout.enabled set to false in prod-config-store.
   - [ ] Canary routing policy created: regional affinity + 10% sample.
3) Telemetry & gating
   - [ ] Baseline capture: snapshot p95 latency, error-rate, token-cost for last 7d saved (snapshot id: radial-baseline-2026-09-27).
   - [ ] Alert runbook updated: latency p95 > 1.8x baseline or 5xx spike > 0.5% -> AUTO-HOLD.
4) Smoke tests & data
   - [ ] Staging smoke with recorded-corpus (corpus tag: radial-smoke-v2) passes end-to-end.
   - [ ] Canary prompt set loaded into canary monitors in SLO panel.
5) People & comms
   - [ ] Lunch-and-go / on-call roster for 48h filled (on-call: Priya, shift: Jonas 08:00-16:00, Elena 16:00-00:00, backup: Samir).
   - [ ] Slack channel #radial-rollout created and participants paged.
6) Customer-facing
   - [ ] Draft release notes below reviewed by product (requested: product-review@redwood.com).

7-day calendar snapshot (high level)
- Day -3 (2026-09-29): Finalize PRs, run canary smoke in staging.
- Day -2 (2026-09-30): Dry-run: execute rollout steps in a simulated cluster.
- Day -1 (2026-10-01): Preflight signoffs, QA approval, reserve burst capacity.
- Day 0 (2026-10-02): Launch window 09:00–18:00 UTC; staggered steps starting at 10:00 UTC.
   * 10:00 — enable canary (10%) in us-west1. 10:10 — verify smoke health.
   * 14:00 — ramp to 35% (if no AUTO-HOLD).
   * 18:00 — ramp to 70% (sanity check).
   * 22:00 — ramp to 100% (complete).
- Day +1 (2026-10-03): Monitor stability, sampling of edge traces, begin retro notes.
- Day +2 (2026-10-04): Finish postmortem if any incidents, finalize release notes.

Live gating and decision rules (operator quick guide)
- Hold criteria (any triggers -> hold immediately):
  * sustained p95 latency > 1.8x baseline for 10m
  * 5xx error rate > 0.5% for 5m
  * token-cost per-request increases > 20% sustained for 30m
  * user-facing regression on canary prompt set (quality check failure >= 2 prompts)
- If HOLD:
  * Step 1: Pause further ramps, set radial-rollout.enabled = false for newly sampled sessions.
  * Step 2: Route traffic away from canary region to primary fallback (us-east4).
  * Step 3: Notify on-call, rotate logs and trace window for 1h, open incident tracker RW-2719.
  * Optional: Hotfix can be attempted if root cause obvious and < 45m.

Rollback recipes (quick):
- Fast rollback: flip model-routing to previous stable variant (flag: radial-variant=stable-v14), disable radial-rollout sampling. Expected < 2m to propagate.
- Partial rollback: reduce global sample to 0.1% then to 0% and keep canary region traffic isolated to 0%.
- Emergency shutdown: scale down dedicated pool alpha-3 to zero (operator: infra-ops), then scale up fallback pool. Use only if catastrophic errors observed.

Operational checklist during each ramp step:
- Minute 0: Confirm k8s pod counts, instance health, and no image pull errors.
- Minute 10: Check SLO dashboard for p95, 5xx, token-cost; sample 20 traces from canary.
- Minute 30: Run lightweight eval on canary prompt set (script: tools/run_canary_eval.sh).
- Minute 45: Decision checkpoint — proceed/hold/rollback. Record decision in #radial-rollout and JIRA RW-2741.

Observability notes and queries to validate post-launch:
- Ensure KV cache hit-rate does not drop below baseline (baseline 86%).
- Watch batching distribution histogram — goal: median batch size within 15% of staging distribution.
- Token cost: compare per-request token consumption to baseline by bucket.
- Trace sampling: 10% sampling for canary traces, ensure stack traces captured for all 5xx.

Draft user-facing release notes (raw):
Title: Radial rollout — improved throughput and smarter routing\nSummary: Today we began a staged rollout of routing improvements that reduce end-to-end latency for many inference requests and balance load across our new radial routing policy. You may see rolling availability for a subset of traffic during the rollout window. If you experience an issue, please contact support@redwood.com with trace id.
Notable internal changes:
- Smarter region-aware routing that routes by latency + cost profile.
- Prefix caching improved to reduce repeated tokenization overheads.
- Config updates to batching heuristics that will reduce tail latency on small requests.
Known limitations:
- Very small fraction of customers using strict regional pinning may briefly see different regional routing during canary.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing):
- Should we extend burst capacity from 2h to 4h if any of the early ramps degrade (cost vs safety trade-off)? Pending decision from infra (Samir).
- Final wording for public release notes: product to confirm tone and any customer opt-out guidance.
- Should downstream partners (marketplace vendors) receive an advance note? Compliance check pending.

Post-launch artifacts to produce:
- Final release notes (product)
- Post-launch telemetry package (slices + dashboards) uploaded to Confluence page (link in linked_artifacts).
- Short retro note summarizing decision checkpoints and any incidents (template: retro/radial-YYYYMMDD).

Appendix: quick links and commands
- GH PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5812
- Canary eval script: /infra/tools/run_canary_eval.sh
- Toggle flag CLI: rctl set-flag radial-rollout.enabled false --env prod
- Pager channel: #radial-rollout
- Incident ticket template: RW-2719 (use when opening regressions)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first step short — too slow ramps leave us exposed to long tail regressions.
- If token-cost spikes, correlate to batching distribution first before blaming model variant.
- Remember to capture sample traces with user-agent header for customer follow-up.

End of doc.

(Working draft — please push comments directly in this doc and tag @AveryChen for critical signoffs.)
